acceptance: docs.yml has a concurrency block that cancels superseded pull_request runs only.
A test or workflow lint asserts push runs on develop and release are never cancel-in-progress.
On a PR with two quick pushes, the first docs run is cancelled and the second completes.
Post-landing note reports docs PR runner-minutes for 7 days, measured from the Actions jobs API.
context:
Landed in #2160 on 2026-09-17. Post-landing measurement, 2026-09-17 to 2026-09-24, from the Actions runs API.

`docs.yml` pull_request runs in the window: 299 total - 237 success, 20 failure, 42 cancelled, 1 still running. The 42 cancellations are superseded runs ending early instead of completing, which is the saving this item was opened for; at the sampled ~19 runner-minutes per full PR run they account for roughly 800 runner-minutes not spent. That figure is derived from the pre-change per-run sample rather than summed job time for each cancelled run, so treat it as an estimate.

Configuration verified in `.github/workflows/docs.yml`: pull_request runs share the group `docs-pr-{number}` with `cancel-in-progress` true, while push and workflow_dispatch runs each take a unique per-SHA group with cancellation disabled, so develop and release pushes can never cancel each other and the deploy path is unaffected. The contract is asserted by `tests/unit/workflows/test_docs_concurrency.py`.

The path filter and job content were left unchanged, and Documentation remains a non-required check, so no ruleset change was needed. Failure causes are owned by ci-dedupe-08.
description:
`.github/workflows/docs.yml` has no `concurrency` block, and it is the only large PR workflow without one. Its path filter includes `benchbox/**`, `scripts/**`, and `Makefile`, so it runs on nearly every code PR push, and every superseded run finishes. A sampled PR run used about 19 runner-minutes (Sphinx build 14, linkcheck 2, visual regression 3). It ran on 662 PRs between 2026-08-23 and 2026-09-16.

Change: add a concurrency group that cancels in-progress `pull_request` runs for the same PR when a newer push arrives.
